jobs.title: Firmware Engineer II
jobs.description: **About Us** ------------ Epia Neuro is a neural technology company developing intent\-driven systems designed to restore function and independence for people living with neurological conditions. Its platform integrates implantable neural interfaces, adaptive algorithms, and assistive devices to translate neural intent into real\-world action. The company's initial focus is stroke\-related motor impairment, with expansion into cognitive decline and other neurological disorders, focusing on long\-term solutions for the growing aging population. **The Role** ------------ We're looking for a Firmware Engineer II who is passionate about developing and testing embedded software for medical devices. You'll contribute to the design, implementation, and testing of firmware for our implantable neural interfaces and external devices, working across the embedded software development lifecycle—from hardware bring\-up and device drivers to application development, integration, and verification. This is a hands\-on engineering role combining strong technical skills with exceptional attention to detail. You'll work closely with hardware, software, and research teams to build robust embedded systems that meet the demanding requirements of regulated medical devices. **What You'll Do** ------------------ *Embedded Firmware Development* * Design, develop, test, and maintain embedded firmware in C/C\+\+ for implantable and external medical devices. * Develop device drivers, communication interfaces, and application\-level firmware for microcontroller\-based systems. * Implement firmware features involving hardware peripherals, real\-time operation, custom ASICs, and communication protocols. * Develop Python scripts and applications to interface with embedded devices for testing, debugging, and characterization. * Participate in firmware design discussions and code reviews, contributing to software quality, reliability, and maintainability. *Hardware Integration \& Testing* * Support hardware bring\-up, firmware integration, and troubleshooting of embedded systems. * Debug hardware and firmware issues using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG/SWD debuggers, and other laboratory equipment. * Develop and execute unit tests, integration tests, and automated tests to verify firmware functionality and reliability. * Collaborate with hardware, software, and research teams to integrate firmware with the broader medical\-device system. *Regulated Development \& Documentation* * Develop firmware within our regulated quality management system and software lifecycle, contributing to requirements, design, verification, and documentation consistent with ISO 13485 and IEC 62304\. * Document firmware designs, interfaces, test procedures, and verification results to support development and regulatory activities. * Investigate defects, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions to improve firmware quality and reliability. **Qualifications** ------------------ * Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. * 2\+ years of professional experience developing embedded firmware or embedded software. * Strong proficiency in C/C\+\+ for microcontroller\-based embedded systems. * Experience with microcontrollers (e.g., ARM Cortex\-M), hardware peripherals, interrupts, and embedded communication protocols such as UART, SPI, and I2C. * Experience with Python for scripting, automation, or embedded device testing. * Experience debugging embedded systems using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and hardware debuggers. * Ability to read schematics and understand basic digital and analog electronics. * Familiarity with real\-time operating systems (RTOS) and embedded software design principles. * Experience using Git and participating in collaborative software development. * Strong problem\-solving and communication skills, with attention to detail and the ability to independently develop, debug, and test firmware features and collaborate across engineering disciplines. **Nice to Have** ---------------- * Experience with Nordic Semiconductor nRF microcontrollers, the nRF Connect SDK, and Zephyr RTOS. * Experience with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), USB, or other embedded communication interfaces. * Experience developing low\-power, battery\-operated embedded systems. * Experience with automated firmware testing, unit testing frameworks, or CI/CD pipelines. * Experience with static code analysis tools and embedded debugging tools such as Segger J\-Link or GDB. * Experience developing software for medical devices or other regulated or safety\-critical systems. * Familiarity with IEC 62304, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, or medical\-device design controls. * Familiarity with secure firmware development and medical\-device cybersecurity requirements. **Physical Requirements** ------------------------- * Ability to work on site, including hands\-on testing with prototype devices, laboratory equipment, and participation in hardware bring\-up and integration sessions. **How We Work** --------------- * **We are intentional.** We prioritize and are thoughtful about how we use others' time. * **We care for others.** We prioritize safety both for patients and one another. * **We own outcomes, not just tasks.** Our work demands the highest standards because it impacts real patients and real lives. * **Humility is a strength.** We are honest about what we know and what we don't know. Getting it right matters more than being right. **Location** ------------ This role is based in Alameda, CA, on site 5 days a week. **Benefits** ------------ Full\-time employees are eligible for the following benefits: * Competitive base salary with equity * 100% of healthcare coverage for you and your dependents * Generous vacation policy * Paid parental leave * Work from our waterfront office in Alameda, CA, with access to collaborative spaces and labs Compensation Range: $115K \- $140K

architecture specs from product requirements through tape\-out. * Lead design and verification reviews, and follow coding, verification, and methodology standards set by the team. * Mentor junior engineers and provide technical direction across multiple projects. * Lead post\-silicon debug and root\-cause analysis, and feed silicon learnings back into design and verification. * Evaluate and improve design and verification flows and tools to increase team productivity and reuse. * Write and maintain automation scripts for regression testing, build flows, and hardware validation. * verification concepts. * PMIC and power electronics basics: DC\-DC converter control, sequencing, protection and fault handling, trimming, and how digital logic interacts with analog blocks. * and automation. * Attention to detail combined with a pragmatic, schedule\-aware approach. * Comfortable in a smaller team where larger impacts are required **Required Qualifications****Basic*** B.S. SystemVerilog for design \& verification * Solid understanding of ASIC design flows including RTL design, synthesis, timing closure, and verification. * Experience with digital simulation tools (e.g., Xcelium, Questa, Vivado Simulator). * Experience with FPGA development using Xilinx tools (Vivado, ISE) for prototyping and silicon validation. * Proficient in scripting (Python, TCL, Bash, etc.) for automation and test. * Strong digital design fundamentals and hardware debugging skills. * Proficient with versioning software (Git) * Familiarity \& experience in leveraging simulation and verification features * Assertions, Linting, Threading * Metric Driven Verification (Code, Conditional Branch, Toggle, FSM Branch, Functional, etc.) **Preferred*** M.S./PHD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field. * 8\+ years of industry experience in digital hardware design (ASIC, FPGA, or embedded hardware) * Experience designing digital circuits for PMICs, DC\-DC converters, battery management, or other power management products. * Hands\-on experience with standard cell logical synthesis including writing and refining SDC constraints. * Experience with place and route including floor planning, placement, clock tree synthesis, routing, and timing closure. * Experience with static timing analysis and signoff across corners and modes including timing ECOs. * Experience with power integrity analysis * Experience with logical equivalence checking across RTL, synthesized, and post\-layout netlists. * Familiarity with physical verification (DRC/LVS) and working with layout teams to resolve issues. * Experience with DFT insertion and ATPG, and supporting ATE test bring\-up. * Experience with CDC analysis and lint signoff tools. * Multiple successful tape\-outs, ideally on mature mixed\-signal or BCD processes common in power management. * Familiarity with embedding third\-party IP (MCUs, memories, etc.) within network of digital accelerators jobs.title: Staff Applications Engineer (Integrated Voltage Regulators)
jobs.description: **Job Purpose:** Navitas Semiconductor (Nasdaq: NVTS) is a next\-generation power semiconductor leader driving innovation in gallium nitride (GaN) and high\-voltage silicon carbide (SiC) technologies. Our products enable faster, more efficient power delivery across AI data centers, high\-performance computing, energy and grid infrastructure, and industrial electrification. With more than 30 years of combined expertise in wide bandgap technologies, GaNFast™ power ICs integrate GaN power, drive, control, sensing, and protection, delivering faster power delivery, higher system density, and greater efficiency. GeneSiC™ high\-voltage SiC devices leverage patented trench\-assisted planar technology to provide industry\-leading voltage capability, efficiency, and reliability for medium\-voltage grid and infrastructure applications. We are seeking an Applications Engineer \- Integrated Voltage Regulators to join the IVR Business Unit and own the system\-level performance of integrated voltage regulators from the lab bench through customer board evaluation. The role develops evaluation platforms and reference designs, validates IVR performance under customer\-representative conditions, creates application collateral and customer model kits, supports design\-in and bring\-up, and converts customer requirements and field learning into product\-definition and roadmap input. Our IVRs combine power transistors, digital control, inductors, and capacitors to enable Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) and Embedded Power Delivery (EPD) for AI accelerators, GPUs, CPUs, and custom ASICs.**Key Responsibilities and Duties:*** Develop and execute system\-level test plans for single\- and multi\-IVR power delivery under customer\-representative conditions, including load transients, current sharing, power\-delivery\-network impedance, sequencing, protection, and fault response. * Build processor load\-emulation platforms, dynamic load boards, and test vehicles that demonstrate IVR performance before customer silicon is available. * Benchmark IVRs against competing power\-delivery solutions to identify product differentiation, performance gaps, and improvement opportunities. * Use and extend the team’s shared automation framework to deliver repeatable system\-level measurements and data analysis. * Perform board\- and package\-level PDN and power\-integrity analysis, including DC drop, AC impedance, parasitic, decoupling, and transient droop. * Build circuit\- and system\-level IVR models, including control\-loop stability and interactions among parallel regulators, and correlate simulation results with lab measurements. * Assess thermal and mechanical integration with processor cooling solutions in collaboration with thermal specialists. * Define, design, bring up, and validate evaluation boards and reference designs, working with internal and external PCB designers from schematic and layout requirements through system validation. * Deliver complete design packages, including schematics, layout guidelines, bills of materials, test procedures, measured results, and configuration of GUIs or scripts. * Develop scalable multi\-IVR demonstration platforms for high\-current processor applications. * Lead customer evaluations and design\-ins with xPU vendors, hyperscalers, and ODMs by reviewing architectures, schematics, layouts, package and board stack\-ups, identifying risks, and supporting bring\-up and debug. * Collaborate with OSATs, substrate suppliers, and embedded\-component PCB fabricators to enable IVR integration in vertical and embedded power\-delivery designs. * Author application notes, design and layout guides, datasheet application content, design calculators, and customer model kits covering circuit simulation, PDN, and thermal behavior. * Present customer technical reviews, train sales and field teams, position IVR technology within the grid\-to\-xPU power chain and translate customer requirements and field learning into product\-definition and roadmap input. **Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Other Characteristics (KSAO’s)*** Deep knowledge of DC\-DC conversion, particularly synchronous and multiphase buck regulators and high\-current point\-of\-load power delivery. * Ability to analyze control\-loop stability, transient response, efficiency, current sharing, sequencing, protection, and fault behavior. * Hands\-on proficiency with oscilloscopes, current probes, electronic loads, power analyzers, and network analyzers for loop\-gain and impedance measurements in low\-voltage, high\-current systems. * Ability to correlate circuit, PDN, thermal, and system simulations with laboratory measurements. * Strong understanding of PDN and power\-integrity fundamentals, including parasitic, decoupling, high\-current distribution, package interactions, and board stack\-up effects. * Ability to define schematics, review/perform PCB layouts, and bring up and debug complex power hardware. * Proficiency in Python\-based lab automation and data analysis, with working knowledge of version control such as Git. * Clear technical writing skills for application notes, design guides, datasheet content, test reports, and customer\-facing documentation. * Confident customer communication and presentation skills, with the ability to work across engineering, sales, field, packaging, substrate, PCB, and product teams. * Self\-motivated, hands\-on working style with sound technical judgment and the ability to execute effectively in a fast\-growing, collaborative environment. **Required Qualifications****Basic*** BS in Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. * At least 5 years of experience in power\-electronics design, systems engineering, or semiconductor applications engineering. Levels may be adjusted to Senior Staff level based on depth and scope of experience. * Demonstrated experience with synchronous or multiphase buck regulators, high\-current point\-of\-load systems, control\-loop stability, transient performance, and efficiency optimization. * Hands\-on experience using power\-electronics laboratory instrumentation in low\-voltage, high\-current systems. * Circuit simulation experience using SIMPLIS, SIMetrix, LTspice, PLECS, or equivalent, including correlation of simulation with measurement. * Experience defining schematics, reviewing PCB layouts, and bringing up and debugging power hardware. * Track record of producing clear technical documentation and presenting technical results to customers or cross\-functional teams. * Willingness to travel for customer engagements, on\-site bring\-ups, and industry events. **Preferred*** MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering with emphasis in power electronics, power management, or power integrity. * Experience with integrated voltage regulators, Vertical Power Delivery, Embedded Power Delivery, or advanced point\-of\-load architectures for AI accelerators, GPUs, CPUs, or ASICs. * Customer\-facing semiconductor applications or design\-in experience with hyperscalers, xPU vendors, or ODMs. * Experience with PDN and power\-integrity tools such as Ansys Q3D and/or SIwave, Cadence Sigrity, or Keysight ADS, and thermal tools such as Ansys Icepak, COMSOL, Simcenter Flotherm, or Cadence Celsius. * Knowledge of advanced packaging, package\-level power distribution, embedded components, or substrate co\-design. * Experience with digitally controlled multiphase regulators, current sharing, and interfaces such as PMBus, I2C, I3C, AVSBus, or processor VID protocols. * Familiarity with data\-center power architectures, including OCP rack power and intermediate\-bus converters, and with GaN or SiC power stages. * Working knowledge of semiconductor\-device characterization and statistical analysis is sufficient to support product\-engineering activities. **What We Offer*** **A front\-row seat to the future of power electronics.** Work on cutting\-edge GaN, SiC and integrated voltage regulator technologies that are transforming AI data centers, electrification, and global energy infrastructure. * **A fast\-paced, high\-energy environment**. We move quickly, make decisions with purpose, and empower employees to take ownership and drive real impact from day one. * **A team that shows up and delivers.** We care deeply about our mission, our customers, and each other. We collaborate, support one another, and bring intensity and accountability to everything we do. * **Full support to succeed.** You’ll have access to leadership, cross\-functional collaboration, and the resources needed to innovate and execute at a high level. * **Competitive total rewards.** Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage, unlimited PTO, and a competitive compensation package including base salary, bonus, and equity awards.

jobs.title: Staff Product Engineer (Integrated Voltage Regulators)
jobs.description: **Job Purpose:** Navitas Semiconductor (Nasdaq: NVTS) is a next\-generation power semiconductor leader driving innovation in gallium nitride (GaN), high\-voltage silicon carbide (SiC) and integrated voltage regulator ( IVR) technologies. Our products enable faster, more efficient power delivery across AI data centers, high\-performance computing, energy and grid infrastructure, and industrial electrification. With more than 30 years of combined expertise in wide bandgap technologies, GaNFast™ power ICs integrate GaN power, drive, control, sensing, and protection, delivering faster power delivery, higher system density, and greater efficiency. GeneSiC™ high\-voltage SiC devices leverage patented trench\-assisted planar technology to provide industry\-leading voltage capability, efficiency, and reliability for medium\-voltage grid and infrastructure applications. We are seeking a Staff Product Engineer \- Integrated Voltage Regulators to join the IVR Business Unit and own device characterization and datasheet development from first silicon through production release. This hands\-on role converts product requirements into defensible electrical specifications, builds automated characterization benches, establishes repeatable measurement and data\-quality practices, and partners with test engineering to carry verified limits into wafer sort and final test. The Product Engineer will also help establish the IVR characterization laboratory and the methods used to measure, document, qualify, and release current and future products.**Key Responsibilities and Duties:*** Define and execute device\-characterization plans across input voltage, output voltage, load, temperature, and process corners, including skew lots, documented coverage, sample sizes, pass/fail criteria, and specification traceability. * Measure efficiency, regulation, ripple and noise, load\-transient response, startup and shutdown, sequencing, protection and fault behavior, telemetry accuracy, and device\-level current sharing. * Characterize integrated inductors versus current, frequency, and temperature, and integrated capacitors versus bias and temperature. * Characterize thermal performance, including thermal\-resistance metrics, derating, and safe operating area for placement beneath or within processor packages. * Specify, build, automate, and maintain low\-voltage, high\-current characterization benches supporting fast\-slew load steps, Kelvin sensing, loop\-gain and output\-impedance measurement, and temperature forcing. * Develop characterization boards and fixtures and contribute to the shared test\-automation framework and characterization database. * Establish calibration, measurement\-uncertainty, and data\-quality practices that produce repeatable results across benches and engineers. * Own the product datasheet end to end, including electrical specification tables, test conditions, typical performance curves, pin and functional descriptions, timing diagrams, revision control, and release. * Work with design, technical marketing, and test engineering to set defensible limits, distinguish typical from guaranteed values, and document whether each specification is verified by bench characterization, ATE, or design analysis. * Partner with test engineering on ATE coverage, production limits, guardbands, and bench\-to\-ATE correlation at wafer sort and final test, including known\-good\-die strategy for IVRs embedded in substrates or boards. * Define production trim, calibration, and configuration flows, including telemetry calibration and non\-volatile memory programming. * Provide characterization data for qualification and reliability activities, new\-product introduction, yield improvement, and product or process change assessments. * Lead root\-cause investigations with design, packaging, operations, quality, and reliability teams, including customer returns and failure analysis. **Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Other Characteristics (KSAO’s)*** Strong knowledge of switching regulators, converter control and stability, and analog and mixed\-signal circuit behavior. * Hands\-on proficiency with oscilloscopes, differential and current probes, precision meters, programmable power supplies, electronic loads, and temperature\-forcing systems. * Ability to make accurate measurements in jobs.title: VP, Compute
jobs.description: **Built to set the gold standard for integrated AI infrastructure** Crux AI is a newly formed, U.S.\-based integrated AI infrastructure company created to remove the physical and operational constraints on consequential AI ambitions. Crux brings together power, high\-density data centers, TPU silicon, networking, orchestration software, and ongoing operations as one integrated system. Crux is being capitalized to plan every layer together, develop each one to demanding standards, and operate the whole system with efficiency and reliability. That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI\-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create. **WHAT YOU'LL DO** You will own compute at Crux: the platform that turns Google TPUs, Crux power and data center capacity, and our network into dedicated, reliable, customer\-ready AI compute. Reporting to our CTPO, you own everything between the rack and the customer's first job: the TPU cluster fleet, the software that provisions, monitors and heals it, the container orchestration layer that schedules work onto it, and the compute products our customers consume, from our first phase of capacity through a multi\-gigawatt fleet. This is a platform\-builder seat: you will set the architecture of record, hire the leaders, and hold the bar for reliability, efficiency, and speed as Crux scales. **In this role, you will:** * Define the compute platform strategy and architecture of record: how TPU capacity is carved into dedicated clusters, provisioned, isolated, and delivered to hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, and enterprises. * Architect and deliver the full compute lifecycle: hardware onboarding and inventory, OS and firmware provisioning, burn\-in and validation, rack certification, customer handoff, repair and retirement. * Design and ship Crux's managed container orchestration on bare metal: automated control\-plane provisioning, upgrades, and operators for TPUs. * Build and lead a multi\-layer engineering organization spanning cluster provisioning and lifecycle, orchestration and scheduling, fleet health and telemetry, and the customer\-facing compute surface. * Hire people better than you at their craft, then stay close enough to know when something is off before it shows up in a report. * Own compute reliability and efficiency end to end: SLOs, goodput and utilization, time from rack\-ready to customer\-ready, and failure recovery at fleet scale, achieved through discipline, not heroics. * Serve as Crux's primary technical counterpart to Google on the TPU hardware, software, and services roadmap, translating customer needs into Google requirements and Google capabilities into Crux product. * Set the build, adopt, or integrate line for the compute software stack: what Crux builds natively, what it adopts from Google, and what it sources from partners. * Stand up the security, tenant isolation, and compliance posture that sovereign and regulated customers require for dedicated compute. * Partner with Data Center Engineering and Capacity Delivery on cluster design, bring\-up, and acceptance; with Network Engineering on fabric and interconnect; with TPM's on what we can commit to and when; and with Finance on the utilization, failure\-rate, and spares inputs to the cost and margin model of record. **SIGNALS OF SUCCESS** **After 60 days in this role:** * Gained a complete understanding of the TPU platform, the Google partnership model, the capacity plan of record, and our first customer commitments, and published a written compute architecture and org plan. * Hired or committed your first layer of engineering leaders across the core compute domains. * Established working cadences with Google counterparts, Data Center Engineering, Network Engineering, and our customers’ engineering and product teams. * Adapted to a fast\-paced environment, triaging appropriately and continuously improving our function. * Stood up AI\-forward development of the zero\-touch provisioning, orchestration and observability stack **After 6 months:** * Delivered the first production TPU clusters through provisioning, validation, and customer handoff on the committed timeline. * Defined and instrumented compute SLOs, utilization, and time\-to\-capacity metrics, reviewed weekly in a format the executive team trusts. * Shipped the first version of the customer\-facing compute surface (access, APIs, observability) that customers use without hand\-holding. * Demonstrated an AI\-forward and automated approach to this role: you have built, in a hands\-on way, AI\-enabled tools for fleet operations that the team uses every day. **After 1 year:** * Running a multi\-site TPU fleet at the reliability and efficiency targets committed to customers, with incidents becoming rarer and more boring. * Built a high\-performing compute organization with strong leaders in every domain and a hiring bar that holds as the team grows. * Made the compute platform a differentiator in customer wins and renewals, with the roadmap for the next phases of capacity agreed with Google and the executive team. **EXPERIENCES, ATTRIBUTES AND MINDSET THAT INDICATE A GOOD MATCH** **Experiences** * 15\+ years building and operating large\-scale compute or cloud infrastructure platforms, including 7\+ years leading organizations of organizations at the SVP level or above. * Direct ownership of a production compute platform at scale, such as a hypervisor or virtualization platform, a bare metal or dedicated cloud, a hyperscale compute service, or accelerator (TPU, GPU, or custom silicon) infrastructure, with accountability for reliability and customer outcomes. * A track record of leading a platform rebuild or transformation (on\-prem to cloud, legacy to modern architecture, or a new platform from zero to meaningful revenue) while keeping existing customers running. **Attributes** * You are outcome driven and hands\-on. You can go deep on scheduler design, failure domains, or a provisioning bottleneck with your engineers, then take the same topic to the board. This is a builder's seat, not a supervisory one. * You have owned AI\-first engineering teams, and you make roadmap tradeoffs with customer value, cost, and reliability in the same frame. * You have a high tolerance for ambiguity. You absorb ambiguity and navigate complexity rather than passing it along. **Mindset** * You are skeptical by default. "The cluster is ready" is a hypothesis until it passes acceptance under customer\-shaped load. You build the system that makes the next incident boring. * You operate as an owner, not a supervisor. * You like to build and are not afraid to go deep into engineering implementations * You are AI\-agentic first. Fluent with AI agents, or committed to becoming so quickly, you embed them as first principles in how you and your team work, defaulting to agentic workflows before adding headcount or process. **Nice to have (Preferred, not required):** * Compute leadership at a hyperscaler (Google Cloud, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Meta Infrastructure) or a neocloud (CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe). * Hands\-on exposure to AI accelerators or high\-performance computing: supercomputing, accelerator software stacks, or large training and inference clusters. * Experience building sovereign, distributed, or on\-prem cloud offerings for regulated and government customers. * Experience in both startup and scaled enterprise environments, including building an organization from its first hires. * Standing in open infrastructure communities (for example, Open Compute Project or OpenStack) or patents in systems and infrastructure. **Salary Range Information** The annual salary range for this position has been estimated based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description. **About Crux** * We offer generous base, bonus and additional incentive based compensation * Health, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents * Company\-paid life insurance and disability * Full suite of other optional benefits * 401(k) Plan with 4% company match * Hybrid schedule offering four days in\-office collaboration paired with one remote workday for focused, individual work

jobs.title: Head of Tax
jobs.description: **About Arca** -------------- Arca is a wealth management firm built from the ground up with AI. Most people get financial advice that's reactive: an annual check\-in, a plan that's a document instead of a living thing, a relationship where you're one of three hundred clients your advisor is trying to remember. We think that's backwards. The kind of service that used to require a team of specialists behind you, the kind that makes you feel like the only person in the room, should be available to far more than the ultra\-wealthy. So we're building it. We're not SaaS — we are the wealth management business, rebuilding it from the inside with AI. Our platform is an Iron Man suit for advisors: it takes over the low\-leverage work so they can focus on what actually requires a human, showing up with empathy, context, and judgment. Underneath, it keeps a living understanding of each client. It remembers the thing you mentioned once, six months ago. It notices when your life changes — a new job, a new kid, a market shift — and adjusts before you think to ask. You won't see the technology. You'll just notice your advisor seems to know you better than any financial professional ever has. That's the product we're growing: client by client, on the strength of the experience itself. We started by acquiring firms managing over $1B in client assets, which gave us real advisors, real clients, and real financial outcomes to build against from day one. But acquisition was the starting line. The bet is that an advisor backed by this platform delivers something good enough that clients come to us on their own. It's a $20T market, and we think it's ready to be rebuilt. — Rron, CEO **The receipts** ---------------- * **Stage:** Series A, $64M raised * **Backed by:** General Catalyst, Index Ventures, Venrock * **Board \& Advisors:** Former CEO of Vanguard, Former CFO of Schwab, Founder of Altruist, Morgan Housel (author of The Psychology of Money), Will Guidara (former co\-owner of Eleven Madison Park and author of Unreasonable Hospitality) **The team** ------------ We’re small on purpose and engineering heavy: about 80% of the team is technical. We’re based in NYC and hail from high growth startups like Stripe, Ramp, Rippling, Plaid, Doordash, and Glean. We’re fully in\-office in Flatiron, five days a week—lunch together, coffee breaks, basketball games, happy hours. **The role** ------------ As Arca's Head of Tax, you'll build our tax practice from zero — the first tax hire, with a blank page and a mandate to make tax a proactive part of clients' financial life. Tax is where most of our clients feel the most friction, feel the most uncertain, and get the least help. A scramble for documents every spring, a preparer who sees one year at a time, and a wealth advisor who's never quite looped in. We think tax should be continuous, coordinated with the rest of the plan, and done ahead of the deadline instead of after it. You're here to build an AI\-native tax practice from day one including the document gathering process, return preparation and review, client projection/planning before a client thinks to ask, and more. You'll design what the agents do, where a professional's judgment has to step in, and ensure end\-to\-end quality. This is a hands\-on role involving return preparation, directly helping clients on their most complex situations, partner closely with our wealth advisors so tax and investment advice move as one, and own the service as a business: pricing, revenue, capacity, and the team you'll hire behind you. Most of your time goes to two things: doing the tax work and designing the platform that does it better, sitting next to the engineers who build it. **What you’ll own** ------------------- * **The tax practice.** What we offer — starting with individual returns (1040s) and year\-round planning, projections, and notices, and expanding to business returns (S\-corps and other entity returns) for clients who own businesses — who it's for, and the standard every engagement is held to. You set the scope, the service model, the quality bar as well as selecting vendors (core tax return software in particular) to enable the business. * **An AI\-native tax process.** End\-to\-end design of how tax work gets done at Arca — document collection, data normalization, preparation, review, filing, and post\-filing. You'll work side by side with engineering and product to build it, and be the domain authority on every workflow. * **Clients.** You prepare, review, and own returns for clients whose situations take real expertise: stock options and RSUs, business income, S\-corp owners, rental real estate, and multi\-state filings. You explain tax in plain English and give clients confidence their needs are handled. * **Partnership with our wealth advisors.** Tax and investment advice as one plan, not two silos. You work with advisors on tax\-loss harvesting, Roth conversions, charitable strategy, equity comp exercise timing, and with  the kinds of questions the first year of this practice has to answer.* * **Tax season without the scramble.** We already manage client accounts and know most of their financial picture. What does it take to have 80% of a return assembled before a client uploads a single document — and how do agents chase the remaining 20% seamlessly? * **Where the agent stops and the professional starts.** An agent can reconcile a 1099\-B in seconds. It probably shouldn't be the one deciding how to treat a messy ISO disqualifying disposition. Drawing that line, and building a review layer that makes AI\-prepared work more reliable than the traditional kind, is the core design problem. * **Tax as a year\-round signal.** A client gets a bonus, sells a rental, or exercises options in July. How does the platform notice, rerun the projection, and get the right recommendation in front of the advisor while there's still time to act? * **One plan, two disciplines.** Every rebalance has a tax consequence, and every tax decision changes the investment plan. Designing how tax and wealth advice move together, inside one system, is what makes the model work. **The kind of person who thrives here** --------------------------------------- *You’re excited by ownership, ambiguity, and building things that matter.* * **You're a licensed tax professional.** Active CPA license required, with 8–15\+ years in individual and high\-net\-worth tax experience at a top firm, family office, or planning\-focused practice. You've prepared and reviewed complex 1040s yourself and signed off on others' work. Equity compensation, rental real estate, and multi\-state are familiar ground, and you're comfortable with the business returns that come with owner\-clients: S\-corps, partnerships, and C\-corps. * **You're a change agent.** You've stood up a practice, introduced a new service line, or materially improved ways of operating. You take initiative, operate independently, and have driven impact and results. * **You're AI\-pilled.** You already use AI in your work and have strong opinions on which parts of the tax process it should own. You don't need to write code; you need to know exactly what's slow, what's error\-prone, and what a great system would do instead — and enjoy working next to the engineers who build it. * **Clients and advisors trust you.** You can sit with a client and make a complicated situation feel simple, and you see wealth advisors as partners. Experience working alongside a wealth management or RIA practice is a big plus. * **You hold a high bar because of what's at stake.** This is people's money, their filings, and their standing with the IRS. "Good enough" means something different when a mistake shows up as a notice in someone's mailbox. * **You're someone people actually want to be in the room with.** This is a small team, one office, five days a week, working on problems that don't have clean answers. Kind, direct, and low\-ego, you can give candid feedback without being a jerk, and you're genuinely energized by this environment. **Why now is the moment to join** --------------------------------- *This is a narrow window with unusually high leverage.* * **You're the first.** No legacy process, no inherited tools, no one else's practice to fix. Whoever takes this on defines tax at Arca. * **The clients are already here.** We have real advisors and over $1B in client assets on the platform, and more firms and advisors joining. You're building a practice with demand on day one. * **The platform is live.** Agents already do real work for our advisors. You get to extend a working system into tax rather than wait for one to be built. * **Tax is the next chapter.** As Arca expands from wealth management into tax, estate planning, insurance, and beyond, tax is the first step. The patterns you set become the template for every service line after it. **Benefits:** Medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k), and more. Compensation Range: $175K \- $250K

jobs.title: Scientist, Cell Biology
jobs.description: **Description:** Build human cell models and multiplexed high\-content assays that reveal how drugs cause toxicity and predict their effects in people. Partner with robotics engineers, computational scientists, and ML researchers to generate large\-scale biological datasets that power frontier AI agents for translational drug discovery. **About Axiom:** Axiom’s mission is to eliminate unexpected drug toxicity and unlock an abundance of ultra safe medicines. We are starting with the liver, where toxicity remains a leading cause of drug failure. Our high\-throughput human liver safety platform combines advanced human cell systems with imaging, transcriptomics, mass spectrometry, and drug metabolism measurements. Our AI agents integrate these data with chemical structure, human exposure, and thousands of clinical reference compounds to predict whether a drug will be toxic in humans, why, and how to make it safer. We work with seven of the world’s top twenty pharmaceutical companies to design safety into molecules from the earliest stages. This applied work feeds directly into our partnerships with leading frontier AI labs, turning real discovery challenges and experimental feedback loops into scientific skill trees and reinforcement learning environments that train increasingly superhuman scientists. We then deploy these frontier models to make cancer therapies safer, unlock treatments for chronic diseases that demand exceptional safety, revive promising drugs abandoned because of toxicity, and much more. Our ultimate ambition is to build a superhuman AI agent that predicts how a drug will behave across all major human organ systems before the first patient receives it. With insanely accurate safety predictions, we aim to enable rapid, high\-throughput testing of novel drugs in humans with zero risk of toxicity. This is the key to unlocking an abundance of ultra safe, effective medicines. **What you will do:** * Build human cell models that accurately predict drug\-induced toxicity in the liver, kidney, heart, immune system, and pharmacokinetics like exposure and metabolisms. * Design and optimize physiologically relevant systems using primary human cells, multicellular cultures, organoids, and other advanced models. * Develop high\-content assays that reveal how drugs disrupt cellular function and cause injury. * Combine live\-cell imaging, transcriptomics, proteomics, and mass spectrometry to connect changes in cell behavior with underlying molecular mechanisms. * Work with robotics engineers to build a generalizable robotics platform for assay development and turning complex assays into reproducible, high\-throughput experimental workflows. * Establish rigorous validation and quality control standards to ensure consistent results across cell batches, plates, operators, and laboratories. * Investigate mechanisms of drug\-induced injury and design experiments that distinguish meaningful biological effects from measurement artifacts. * Partner with computational scientists and drug discovery teams to generate large\-scale biological datasets with the quality and depth needed to predict toxicity and guide drug development. * Partner with leading pharmaceutical companies and AI labs to interpret Axiom’s data, uncover the biochemical mechanisms behind observed effects, and guide drug discovery decisions. **What we look for:** * You’re an exceptional experimental scientist with a deep understanding of cell biology and human physiology. * You invent and refine biological models and assays to answer questions that established protocols cannot. * You care deeply about reproducibility, biological relevance, and data quality, with the attention to detail needed to catch subtle sources of error. * You hold your work to extremely rigorous scientific standards, designing decisive experiments with strong controls and drawing conclusions supported by the evidence. * You can interpret complex biological phenotypes and distinguish meaningful effects from noise, confounding factors, and experimental artifacts. * You challenge the limits of conventional cell models and develop systems that better predict human biology and drug responses. * You’re deeply curious about cell biology, experimental technologies, and drug discovery, and eager to master new methods. * You communicate complex science clearly, make a compelling case for your ideas, and inspire scientists and collaborators to pursue ambitious questions. **Technical skills we value:** * Experience with primary human cell culture, iPSC culture and differentiation, and cell engineering. * Experience developing physiologically relevant models, including co\-cultures, organoids, spheroids, and engineered tissues. * A strong foundation in cell biology, molecular biology, physiology, and pharmacology. * Expertise in high\-content imaging, Cell Painting, fluorescence microscopy, live\-cell imaging, and image\-based phenotypic screening. * Experience developing, miniaturizing, and automating assays for high\-throughput screening. * Experience measuring cell viability, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, ER stress, apoptosis, inflammation, and other functional responses. * Familiarity with RNA sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and methods that combine multiple biological measurements. * Strong experimental design and quantitative analysis skills, including dose\-response analysis, statistical methods, assay validation, and quality control.

translate complex business and technical requirements into clear specifications for Alpaca's global engineering team. * Serve as the product and technical subject matter expert, capable of thoroughly understanding and articulating all aspects of the Alpaca platform to diverse audiences and stakeholders. * Work closely with local compliance and operations teams to understand local and regional product requirements. * Own technical sales engagement end\-to\-end: discovery calls, solution validation, RFPs, and security questionnaires that win deals; jobs.title: Manager, Applied AI Engineer
jobs.description: **Description** **About Alvarez \& Marsal** Alvarez \& Marsal (A\&M) is a global consulting firm with entrepreneurial, action\- and results\-oriented professionals. We take a hands\-on approach to solving our clients' problems and helping them reach their potential. A\&M is different by design: we give people ownership and impact from day one, fuel development through real opportunity, and provide direct access to leaders who invest in our growth. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact clients and shape our industry. Guided by A\&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity, our collaborative, globally minded environment is why our people love working at A\&M. **The Team** The AI Lab Team sits within A\&M's Global AI \& Knowledge Organization (GAIKO). GAIKO brings together the firm's AI and Knowledge Management capabilities to put trusted, governed AI into everyday consulting work. The Lab's job is to turn repeatable business workflows into scalable agents and AI skills. Many of these workflows run today on Microsoft tools such as SharePoint, Power Platform and Power BI, and the pod reworks them into AI\-first solutions that can be reused across the firm. Others will be built from scratch as internal teams bring new requests. In this role, you'll work closely with the leads of A\&M's business units, the Knowledge Management (KM) and Data team leads, and the AI Skills lead and engineers, product partners and knowledge specialists across GAIKO. Together you'll design and build headless skills and agents: reusable capabilities that work behind the scenes and connect to the AI tools our professionals already use. You'll be the bridge between the business and the build: translating what each business unit needs into working skills and agents, and teaching the rest of the pod to do the same. As the pod's go\-to technical expert for skills and agents, you'll report to the AI Skills Pod lead with technical direction from the Intelligence Layer tech lead. Your work will directly shape how thousands of A\&M colleagues use AI in their work with clients. The team is growing, the work is technically demanding, and priorities will move quickly, so this role requires sound judgment, adaptability, and a willingness to contribute wherever the build needs support. We're looking for a fast builder who can take an idea from prototype to working capability quickly, learn from feedback and keep momentum without sacrificing quality. Just as important, you make the people around you better. You teach, share knowledge openly, step in across workstreams when needed, and adjust quickly when priorities shift. **How You Will Contribute** * Own end\-to\-end delivery of applied AI solutions, from proof of concept to production: problem framing, build, deployment, monitoring and iteration. * Partner with business unit leaders and their teams to understand how they work, translate their needs into skills and agents, and agree clear success metrics. * Work with the Knowledge Management and Data team leads to gather and clarify requirements, and translate them into skill and agent designs. * Partner with our Data Engineering, BIU, and Intelligence Layer teams so that solutions are built on reliable, production\-grade data. * Design, build and operate headless skills and agentic workflows, including multi\-step orchestration, tool routing, retrieval, guardrails, evaluation and human\-in\-the\-loop controls. * Build and maintain automated skill\-building pipelines (templates, scaffolding, testing and evaluation harnesses, packaging and deployment) so new skills can be created and released quickly and consistently. * Build integrations with large language model platforms and use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to make skills available to approved AI tools and the Intelligence Layer. * Integrate structured and unstructured content from enterprise systems while preserving source permissions, metadata and governance requirements. * Guide the team in assessing current Power Platform and wider Microsoft stack processes, reimagining them as AI\-first workflows rather than one\-to\-one rebuilds, and converting them into, or connecting them to, skills and agents. * Train the wider team on how to build skills, through workshops, playbooks, templates, worked examples and office hours. * Mentor engineers through pairing, code and design reviews and hands\-on coaching, raising the quality bar for skills and agents across the pod. * Apply and help shape engineering standards for skills and agents, working with the Intelligence Layer tech lead, including evaluation, CI/CD, versioning, reproducibility and performance monitoring. * Bring forward recommendations on tools, frameworks and design patterns. Technical decisions are made by the Intelligence Layer tech lead together with the Intelligence Layer lead. * Support responsible AI use, including data privacy, client co pting, evaluation and agentic patterns * Demonstrated track record of designing, building and shipping multiple AI agents and skills into production (examples or a portfolio will be discussed at interview) * Experience building automated pipelines for creating, testing, evaluating and deploying skills or agents at scale * Hands\-on experience with MCP, agent frameworks (for example, Claude Agent SDK, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel or similar) and reusable skill design * Experience with CI/CD, testing and observability for production systems **Nice to Have** * Experience with the Microsoft stack (SharePoint Online, Power Platform, Fabric/Power BI, Azure), including hands\-on Power Automate and Power Apps experience and the ability to re\-engineer existing flows (strongly preferred) * Experience with SQL and modern data platforms * Experience working in Agile environments such as Scrum or Kanban * Experience in a professional services or consulting environment **Communication, Mentoring and People Skills** * Excellent communicator who explains technical concepts in plain business language and can run discovery sessions with business unit leaders to draw out real requirements * Proven mentor and teacher who has upskilled other engineers or non\-technical colleagues, and enjoys building capability in others * Confident presenting to and facilitating workshops with senior stakeholders * Collaborative team player who builds strong working relationships across teams * Bias toward action: builds quickly, ships often and learns through iteration * High ownership and comfort with ambiguity and shifting priorities * Sound judgment on when to ship, when to iterate and when to stop **Open Items to Confirm (remove before posting)** * Salary band: $140K to $180K (centered at $160K) is proposed; confirm with Talent Acquisition. Expect strong candidates to land in the upper half given the scope. * Experience requirement: confirm 5\+ years (including 2\+ on LLM or agent systems) is right for the Manager level. * Work arrangement: confirm remote, hybrid, or office\-based expectations. **Your journey at A\&M** At A\&M, professional growth is tied directly to performance, not tenure. Our people take on meaningful, hands\-on work supported by a performance development process that rewards contribution and fosters a culture of meritocracy. Stretch roles, evolving business needs, and firm growth create ongoing opportunities for ownership and building new skills, while direct access to senior leaders provides mentorship and real\-time coaching along the way. We also prioritize your wellbeing through comprehensive benefits and resources. Together, these elements create an environment where high\-performing professionals can continue to grow and advance from day one. Regular employees working 30 or more hours per week are also entitled to participate in Alvarez \& Marsal Holdings' fringe benefits consisting of healthcare plans, flexible spending and savings accounts, life, AD\&D, and disability coverages at rates determined periodically as well as a 401(k) retirement savings plan. Provided the eligibility requirements are met, employees will also receive an annual discretionary contribution to their 401(k) retirement savings plan from Alvarez \& Marsal. Additionally, employees are eligible for paid time off including vacation, personal days, seventy\-two (72\) hours of sick time (prorated for part time employees), ten federal holidays, one floating holiday, and parental leave. The amount of vacation and personal days available varies based on tenure and role type. Click here for more information regarding A\&M's benefits programs. The salary range is $140,000 \- $160,000 annually, dependent on several variables including but not limited to education, experience, skills, and geography. In addition, A\&M offers a discretionary bonus program which is based on a number of factors, including individual and firm performance. Please ask your recruiter for details.

jobs.description: **DESCRIPTION** --------------- Amazon Lightsail makes AWS accessible to developers and business customers who want to get their cloud stacks running in seconds without the complexity of traditional infrastructure. As a Software Development Engineer II on the Lightsail team, you will build features and services that simplify compute, storage, networking, and website hosting for customers who need things to just work. The team is expanding quickly, adding new capabilities like website hosting and agent hosting, and you will help shape what comes next. You will work across the full software development lifecycle, from understanding customer problems through design, implementation, testing, deployment, and operations. If you are an engineer who enjoys building products you would actually use yourself, and you want to do that at AWS scale, we would like to talk to you. Key job responsibilities Design and build features for Amazon Lightsail's distributed systems, working in Java, Go, JavaScript, and React across both backend services and frontend experiences. Collaborate with partner teams across AWS — including Amazon EC2, Amazon Route 53, Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3\), Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) — to integrate Lightsail capabilities with the broader AWS ecosystem. Own the operational health of the services you build by identifying root causes of production issues and driving permanent fixes, ensuring customers experience reliable performance. Participate actively in design reviews and code reviews, providing constructive feedback to teammates and mentoring other engineers on writing clean, maintainable code. Evaluate new technologies and approaches, including generative artificial intelligence tools, to improve team productivity and the quality of solutions delivered to customers. A day in the life You start your morning checking operational dashboards for a Lightsail service you recently launched, then join a design review where you and a teammate work through how to integrate a new hosting capability with an existing AWS service. After lunch, you pick up a feature task, writing backend logic in Java and wiring up the React console so customers can try it out. Later, you review a pull request from a teammate, leave detailed feedback, and update documentation so the next engineer who touches this code can ramp up quickly. About the team Amazon Lightsail sits within AWS and has a distinctive mission: make cloud infrastructure simple and approachable for non\-enterprise customers. jobs.description: Join the App Intelligence team and help redefine what a deeply personal and integrated assistant can be. jobs.title: AIML - Machine Learning Engineer, Evaluation - Responsible AI and Safety
jobs.description: Join Us in Shaping the Future of Generative AI at Apple! Are you passionate about making AI systems safer, more inclusive, and globally representative? Apple is seeking an experienced Senior Machine Learning Engineer to help shape the future of responsible AI evaluation for the next generation of generative features. In this role, you will work to assess, quantify, and improve the safety and inclusivity of Apple’s Generative\-AI powered features and products. Your work will tackle innovative problems in machine learning, particularly focused on large language models for text generation, diffusion models for image generation, and mixed model systems for multimodal applications. You will directly influence how we evaluate, align, and monitor the safety of large language and multimodal models, while upholding Apple's values, privacy, and quality standards. As part of Apple’s Responsible AI group within the Software Engineering organization, you’ll collaborate with cross\-functional partners to minimize unintended consequences across people, systems, and society while elevating feature capabilities and the overall user experience. You’ll anticipate safety risks and deliver trusted, high\-quality AI experiences to users around the globe. **Description** We are seeking a visionary Senior Machine Learning Engineer to drive Responsible AI Evaluation efforts for global generative AI products. In this role, you will provide critical technical execution for operationalizing policy and risk assessments into measurable criteria; designing datasets; developing LLM\- and human\-in\-the\-loop methods for data analysis; and implementing robust data pipelines to produce reliable, scalable insights that inform ship/no\-ship product decisions. Pre\- and post\-launch, you will be deeply hands\-on\-analyzing evaluation results, conducting failure investigations, and leveraging human and automated feedback to continuously improve feature safety and build user trust. As a senior technical leader on the team, you will champion technical excellence, empower leadership with data\-driven safety recommendations, and systematically solve complex engineering roadblocks. This role heavily draws on applied data science, scientific investigation, cross\-functional collaboration, and defending safety metrics to stakeholders and decision\-makers. **Preferred Qualifications** Experience working with multimodal models, agentic systems, and/or diverse languages and locales Experience with compliance and regulatory needs in the AI space, specifically regarding child safety, clinical/health applications, or companionship chatbots Experience conducting large scale benchmarking across models and capabilities **Minimum Qualifications** Develop metrics for the evaluation of safety and fairness risks inherent to generative models and Gen\-AI features. Design datasets, identify data needs, and implement creative solutions to scale and expand data coverage through human and synthetic generation methods. Develop sampling strategies and combine human annotation with auto\-grading to deliver high\-quality, high\-confidence insights at a fast pace and large scale. Design, implement, and optimize data pipelines, collaborating cross\-functionally to execute end\-to\-end safety evaluations. Drive operational excellence by automating manual workflows and optimizing evaluation velocity to meet rapid product release cycles. Distill complex project findings into actionable insights for product engineering teams and safety policy development. Work with highly\-sensitive content, including exposure to offensive and controversial material. **Pay \& Benefits** At Apple, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. jobs.title: Clinical Studies Engineer II - Cardiac Rhythm Management (CRM)
jobs.description: Clinical Studies Engineer II \- Cardiac Rhythm Management (CRM) BIOTRONIK is one of the leading manufacturers of cardio\- and endovascular implants and catheters for cardiac rhythm management, electrophysiology and vascular intervention. As a globally active company headquartered in Berlin, Germany, we develop, produce and distribute high\-quality medical products based on the latest technology and research. Our success is based on the competence and results\-oriented cooperation of our employees. BIOTRONIK is seeking an experienced Clinical Studies Engineer II with Cardiac Rhythm Management (CRM) and medical\-device clinical research experience to support clinical investigations involving cardiac rhythm technologies. This role contributes across the clinical study lifecycle, including protocol and case report form development, study initiation and execution, investigative\-site support, clinical data review and analysis, clinical reporting, and regulatory submissions. The Clinical Studies Engineer II serves as a clinical and technical resource for investigators, study sites, field personnel, and internal stakeholders. The position requires existing knowledge of CRM technologies and clinical procedures, along with the ability to apply that expertise to the compliant execution of medical\-device clinical investigations. The role collaborates closely with Clinical Data Operations, Engineering, Research and Development, Advanced Product Support, regulatory partners, and other cross\-functional teams. **Essential Functions:** * Apply and further develop expertise in Cardiac Rhythm Management technologies, associated clinical procedures, and cardiac implantable electronic devices, including pacemakers, implantable cardioverter\-defibrillators (ICDs), and cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) devices. * Participate in all phases of clinical investigations, including study design, initiation, enrollment, execution, data analysis, clinical report writing, and study closeout. * Lead the development and revision of clinical study protocols and design case report forms (CRFs) that support accurate, complete, and protocol\-aligned data collection. * Develop study documents, site and internal training materials, and other resources supporting protocols, investigational devices, study procedures, and CRF completion. * Provide day\-to\-day study management and clinical and technical support to investigative sites, investigators, site coordinators, field clinical personnel, sales representatives, and internal stakeholders. * Train investigative sites and BIOTRONIK personnel on clinical protocols, investigational devices, procedures, and clinical data requirements. * Review and/or monitor CRFs, source documents, and study records in accordance with BIOTRONIK procedures and applicable regulatory requirements. * Partner with study teams, field personnel, and investigative sites to resolve data discrepancies, protocol deviations, compliance concerns, regulatory issues, and operational challenges. * Partner with Clinical Data Operations to clean, organize, summarize, and analyze complex clinical data. * Generate clinical reports, contribute to scientific publications, and support clinical content for FDA submissions. * Participate as a clinical representative in FDA meetings when needed, including presenting and explaining device features, clinical study design, and study results. * Attend device implants and/or follow\-up procedures as needed to maintain current knowledge of cardiac rhythm devices, clinical utilization, and patient care. * Provide clinical and technical feedback to Engineering and Research and Development, contribute to new project planning, and support the training and mentoring of newly hired Clinical Studies Engineers. * Build and maintain effective professional relationships with investigators and investigative sites, and support additional clinical studies or projects as business needs require. **Competencies:** * Working knowledge of FDA regulations, ICH guidelines, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and other standards governing medical\-device clinical research. * Applied knowledge of CRM therapies, devices, terminology, and associated implant and follow\-up procedures. * Ability to translate complex clinical, technical, and study information for investigative sites and cross\-functional stakeholders. * Ability to independently manage multiple priorities and contribute effectively within cross\-functional teams. * Strong clinical study problem\-solving, judgment, organization, and attention to detail. * Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, training, and interpersonal skills. * Ability to work effectively with clinical study data, protocols, CRFs, source documentation, reports, and regulatory content. * Ability to build credibility and productive relationships with investigators, clinical sites, field teams, and internal partners. **Required Education and Experience:** * Bachelor's degree m Management technologies and/or cardiac implantable electronic devices, such as pacemakers, ICDs, or CRT devices. * Demonstrated experience supporting medical\-device clinical investigations and working with investigative sites, clinical study protocols, clinical data, and study documentation. * Working knowledge of FDA regulations, ICH guidelines, GCP, and other applicable clinical research requirements. **Preferred Education and Experience:** * Master's degree in a health profession, biological or life science, engineering, or a related discipline. * Experience supporting Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) clinical studies. * Experience developing clinical study protocols and CRFs. * Experience with clinical data analysis, clinical report writing, and/or scientific publications. * Experience preparing clinical content for FDA submissions or participating in regulatory\-agency interactions. * Clinical or field experience supporting CRM device implants and/or follow\-up procedures. **Supervisory Responsibilities:** This position does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. The employee may support the training and mentoring of newly hired Clinical Studies Engineers. **Work Environment:** This position operates in a professional office and remote\-work environment and routinely uses standard office equipment, including computers and phones. The employee also works in clinical settings, including hospitals and investigative sites, when attending device procedures, conducting training, or supporting clinical investigations. Work location is hybrid from the Lake Oswego, Oregon campus or remote within the United States based on skills and qualifications. **Physical Demands:** The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. * Ability to be independently mobile and travel to clinical sites, procedures, training sessions, and meetings as required. * Ability to interact with a computer for extended periods and communicate effectively with coworkers and external stakeholders. * Ability to perform the essential functions of the role in professional office, remote\-work, hospital, and clinical\-site environments. **Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:** This is a full\-time position requiring a minimum of 40 hours per week. Standard workdays are Monday through Friday. Work hours may vary based on the time zones of supported study sites and business needs; occasional evening or weekend work may be required. **Travel:** Travel is generally limited to less than two weeks per year for clinical procedures, investigative\-site training, and meetings. Depending on study needs and the phase of a clinical investigation, travel may periodically increase to up to 25% and may include overnight travel within the United States. **Additional Eligibility Qualifications:** * Ability to meet BIOTRONIK requirements for access to healthcare facilities and investigative sites, as applicable. * Ability to maintain required training and certifications related to clinical research, product support, and assigned clinical studies. Are you interested? Please apply online through our application management system! We are looking forward to welcoming you. We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. SLIs/SLOs and participate in a minimal on\-call rotation. * Security by Design: Follow secure coding practices and remediate findings; PCI \& SOX awareness is helpful. * Technical Leadership: Lead design reviews, mentor peers, and guide pull requests with a high bar for craftsmanship. * Operate What You Build: Practice build‑it/run‑it ownership from development through production. **Education jobs.title: Environmental / Civil Engineer – Wastewater Treatment & Renewable Energy
jobs.description: Position Summary The Environmental / Civil Engineer will participate in planning, design, permitting, construction oversight, startup, and optimization of wastewater treatment and renewable energy facilities. This hands\-on position combines office\-based engineering design with field engineering and construction management responsibilities. The successful candidate will work directly with engineers, contractors, equipment manufacturers, facility owners, regulatory agencies, and plant operators to deliver projects from initial concept through engineering design, construction, commissioning, and ongoing facility operations. The position will also involve working closely with facility operators to evaluate system performance, troubleshoot operational issues, implement process improvements, and optimize wastewater treatment and renewable energy production. Key ResponsibilitiesWastewater Treatment Engineering · Design and evaluate municipal, industrial, and decentralized wastewater treatment systems. · Develop engineering calculations, process flow diagrams, hydraulic profiles, and mass balances. · Evaluate biological treatment processes, including activated sludge, biological nutrient removal, anaerobic treatment, and advanced treatment technologies. · Design wastewater collection, pumping, storage, treatment, and effluent disposal systems. · Develop groundwater discharge, land application, and soil\-based wastewater dispersal systems. · Evaluate existing treatment facilities and recommend improvements. · Prepare engineering drawings, specifications, design reports, and construction documents. Anaerobic Digestion and Renewable Energy · Support design and optimization of anaerobic digestion systems treating municipal sludge, industrial wastewater, agricultural residuals, and food processing wastes. · Perform calculations involving organic loading rates, hydraulic retention time, volatile solids destruction, methane generation, and biogas production. · Design food waste receiving, storage, preprocessing, and co\-digestion systems. · Evaluate biogas collection, conditioning, storage, and utilization equipment. · Support integration of biogas\-fueled CHP systems into wastewater treatment facilities. · Develop energy and heat recovery calculations. · Evaluate nutrient recovery, biosolids processing, and beneficial reuse. Construction Oversight and Field Engineering · Oversee construction of wastewater treatment facilities, anaerobic digestion systems, renewable energy facilities, and related infrastructure. · Represent engineering interests during construction to help ensure compliance with approved plans, specifications, and applicable requirements. · Coordinate activities with contractors, subcontractors, equipment suppliers, facility owners, and plant operators. · Monitor construction schedules, project progress, workmanship, and specification compliance. · Review submittals, shop drawings, requests for information (RFIs), proposed field modifications, change orders, and payment applications. · Conduct site visits, construction inspections, and progress meetings; prepare observation reports and punch lists. · Resolve field engineering issues and coordinate installation of tanks, pumps, piping, process equipment, mechanical and electrical systems, and energy equipment. · Assist with system testing, equipment startup, commissioning, closeout, and operational troubleshooting. · Promote safe construction practices and coordinate with contractors on identified site safety concerns. Engineering Design and Project Development · Prepare feasibility studies, preliminary engineering reports, conceptual designs, and technical evaluations. · Develop equipment sizing calculations, hydraulic analyses, and engineering cost estimates. · Coordinate civil, mechanical, electrical, and process engineering requirements. · Assist with equipment selection, procurement, and technical evaluations. · Prepare and review AutoCAD drawings and construction documents. · Support project budgeting, construction planning, scheduling, and client coordination. Regulatory Compliance and Permitting · Prepare technical documentation supporting wastewater treatment and environmental permits. · Support permitting with Michigan EGLE and other regulatory agencies. · Assist with wastewater discharge, groundwater discharge, and construction permit applications. · Evaluate compliance with environmental regulations, engineering standards, and permit requirements. · Coordinate with regulatory agencies, facility owners, and project stakeholders. Required Qualifications · Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline. · 3–7 years of relevant engineering experience, preferably in wastewater treatment, environmental engineering, infrastructure development, or facility construction. · Understanding of wastewater treatment processes and environmental engineering principles. · Experience preparing engineering calculations, reports, and design documents. · Experience with or demonstrated ability to perform construction oversight, field engineering, and contractor coordination. · Familiarity with AutoCAD or comparable engineering design software. · Strong analytical, organizational, problem\-solving, and communication skills. · Ability to manage multiple assignments, work collaboratively, and visit active construction sites and operating facilities. · Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to project sites as needed. Preferred Qualifications · Master’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a related discipline. · Engineer\-in\-Training (EIT) certification or Professional Engineer (PE) license, or progress toward licensure. · Experience with municipal or industrial wastewater treatment facility design and construction oversight. · Knowledge of anaerobic digestion, biogas production, and CHP systems. · Experience with contractor coordination, equipment installation, commissioning, and operational troubleshooting. · Experience with process modeling, hydraulic calculations, and mass balance analysis. · Familiarity with Michigan wastewater treatment and groundwater discharge permitting. · Proficiency in AutoCAD Civil 3D, Microsoft Excel, or wastewater process modeling software. Pay: $70,800\.00 \- $98,700\.00 per year Benefits: * 401(k) * Dental insurance * Flexible schedule * Retirement plan Work Location: In person

jobs.description: We're Blue River, a team of innovators driven to create intelligent machinery that solves monumental problems for our customers. Blue River Technology aligns with John Deere's vision to "innovate on behalf of humanity" by quickly identifying and solving high\-value, high\-uncertainty challenges in AI, machine learning, computer vision, and robotics. BRT acts as a research and development flywheel, building not only new products but also new platforms that reliably create value for both Deere and its customers. From fully autonomous machines to highly precise farming equipment, BRT and Deere are partnering to create technical breakthroughs in industries like agriculture and construction.
